# x86_semantics.py cases where Rosetta and an x86 CPU differ: what it left (docs/macos/integer-data/silicon_overrides.py writes this file). One corpus line per family run on the x86 CPU, an AMD EPYC 7763 (raven-macos-bench run 44532999818, assembled with clang as here; dump sha256 f672c276756d52cb1383f944525af03854da94ba467584b202ad2939010def5c): every family, rflags the newest. The tests refuse the file when a family's cases or Rosetta's results change.
# Earlier runs gave the same results for the families they had: AMD EPYC 9V74 runs 44522174773 (random) and 44522713416 (random, multiply, divide), AMD EPYC 7763 runs 44523646082 (and bit test) and 44524257886 (and locked), AMD EPYC 9V45 runs 44526496471 (and group 4) and 44527495718 (and group 5). The random family's one difference, the RAX a 32-bit lock cmpxchg leaves, was first found on an AMD EPYC 9V45 (run 44411803673).
# Rosetta and the EPYCs agree in every register, memory byte and defined flag of every directed family; they differ only in flags x86 leaves undefined (counted by silicon_overrides.py, not written).
